task.question: What is the name of the star reported in August 2026 as the closest and fastest star yet observed orbiting Sagittarius A*?
task.evidence: 19 August – Astronomers report the discovery of S301, the closest and fastest star yet observed orbiting Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way. The star completes an orbit every 8.7 years and reaches about 25,000 km/s, or 8.5% of the speed of light, at its closest approach. Its unusually tight orbit may enable a direct measurement of Sagittarius A*'s spin within about a decade.

S4716 is a star that orbits Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way, completing each orbit in approximately 4 years. In 2022, it was the closest known star to Sagittarius A*.

## Discovery
S4716 was co-discovered by Florian Peißker, a German astrophysicist, and Michael Zajaček, a Czech astrophysicist. The discovery was first published in 2022 in *The Astrophysical Journal*.

## Characteristics
S4716 travels at a minimum speed of approximately 8000 km/s (about 2.7% the speed of light). The star's orbit is highly elliptical. The star was the closest star to Sagittarius A* discovered at the time.
